summary: Client book length mismatch resulting in crash
description: Editing (already once edited) books with colored content makes the client mismatch the actual character length, resulting in either one character too much (takes away another character) or too less ( or following character still left) being deleted when removing characters. Concrete steps to reproduce: - start a 1.13.2 client, create a new singleplayer world, copy and paste any text with characters in a book (see below), save world - start a 1.14.x client, convert open the world, open the book Or use the following command in 1.14.x: setblock oak_sign{Text1:"{ "text ": "Click me ", "clickEvent ":{ "action ": "run_command ", "value ": " give p writable_book{pages:[ " u00a7nVery cool text n u00a7r u00a7 u00a7 u00a7 u00a7 hi n u00a75more n u00a7etext "]} "}}"} What can be observed: - clicking on or marking the last character of the book - crash - going to the last character with the right arrow doesn t go to the very end, but stops at a character before it - trying to remove characters where a is results in seemingly the wrong character being removed - most notably: clicking the front on the second last line, then pressing the delete backspace key removes characters a few letters behind the actually selected position This means that on a click in lines containing the position character length is calculated wrongly i.e. copy and paste nVery cool text r hi 5and even more etext The older 1.14.3 crash log had a different stacktrace , this is the latest 1.15.2: crash-2020-04-28_15.38.46-client.txtjava.lang.StringIndexOutOfBoundsException: String index out of range: 44 at java.base java.lang.StringLatin1.charAt(StringLatin1.java:48) at java.base java.lang.String.charAt(String.java:711) at dch.a(SourceFile:454) at dha.mouseClicked(SourceFile:779) at dbo.b(SourceFile:86) at dgb.wrapScreenError(SourceFile:447) at dbo.a(SourceFile:86) at dbo.c(SourceFile:150) at ais.execute(SourceFile:94) at dbo.b(SourceFile:150) at org.lwjgl.glfw.GLFWMouseButtonCallbackI.callback(GLFWMouseButtonCallbackI.java:36) at org.lwjgl.system.JNI.invokeV(Native Method) at org.lwjgl.glfw.GLFW.glfwPollEvents(GLFW.java:3101) at com.mojang.blaze3d.systems.RenderSystem.flipFrame(SourceFile:98) at cxx.e(SourceFile:301) at dbn.d(SourceFile:1012) at dbn.d(SourceFile:619) at net.minecraft.client.main.Main.main(SourceFile:204)
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft Java Edition 1.13.2.
2. Create a new Singleplayer world.
3. Copy and paste any text with colored characters into a book.
4. Save the world and exit the game.
5. Launch Minecraft Java Edition 1.14.x.
6. Open the previously created world to convert it.
7. Open the book containing the colored text.
8. Click on or mark the last character of the book.
9. Observe that the game crashes.
10. Alternatively, use the command: `setblock oak_sign{Text1:"{ "text ": "Click me ", "clickEvent ":{ "action ": "run_command ", "value ": " give p writable_book{pages:[ " u00a7nVery cool text n u00a7r u00a7 u00a7 u00a7 u00a7 hi n u00a75more n u00a7etext "]} "}}"}`
11. Observe that navigating to the last character with the right arrow does not go to the very end, but stops at a character before it.
12. Attempt to remove characters and observe that the wrong character may be deleted.
Environment: Minecraft Java Edition Versions: 1.14, 1.14.1 Pre-Release 1, 1.14.1 Pre-Release 2, 1.14.1, 1.14.2 Pre-Release 1, 1.14.2 Pre-Release 2, 1.14.2 Pre-Release 3, 1.14.2 Pre-Release 4, 1.14.2, 1.14.3 Pre-Release 1, 1.14.3 Pre-Release 2, 1.14.3 Pre-Release 3, 1.14.3, 1.14.4 Pre-Release 5, 1.14.4 Pre-Release 6, 1.14.4 Pre-Release 7, 1.14.4, 1.15.1, 1.15.2, 20w17a (includes snapshots)
Observed Behavior: When editing books that contain colored text, players experience a mismatch in character length, leading to a crash. This issue arises when characters are deleted from the book, resulting in either an incorrect deletion of one character too many or leaving an extra character behind. To reproduce the bug, players can start a client in version 1.13.2 and create a singleplayer world where they copy and paste text into a book, then save the world. Upon launching a 1.14.x client and converting the world, opening the book reveals the problem. Specifically, when players click on or highlight the last character, the game crashes. Additionally, using the right arrow key to navigate to the last character does not position the cursor at the very end but rather one character before it. Attempting to delete characters can lead to unexpected results, such as removing characters that are not at the intended position. For instance, if a player clicks near the start of the second to last line and presses the backspace key, it may remove characters several letters behind the actual cursor position. This indicates a miscalculation of character length when clicking in lines, particularly with pasted content. The crash log from version 1.15.2 shows a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, which further illustrates the underlying issue with character indexing in the client.
Expected Behavior: When editing a colored book in Minecraft, the client should accurately reflect the character length, allowing players to navigate and modify the text without any discrepancies. Clicking on the last character should position the cursor correctly at the end of the text, and removing characters should delete the intended characters without affecting others. The text should remain stable and functional across versions, ensuring a smooth editing experience.
